findings.title: Hard-coded AWS access keys committed in provider config, EC2 user-data, and Lambda env vars
findings.attack_path: Anyone with read access to the repo or to rendered EC2 user-data / Lambda environment reads AKIA... and the secret key from providers.tf (lines 10-11), ec2.tf user_data (lines 15-16), and lambda.tf environment (lines 45-46), then authenticates to AWS as those principals and pivots across the account.
findings.remediation: Remove all literal AWS keys from source. Use instance profiles / IAM roles, AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store, and rotate any exposed key immediately. Add secret scanning to CI.

findings.title: Hard-coded database admin password as Terraform default and embedded in EC2 user-data
findings.attack_path: var.password defaults to 'Aa1234321Bb' in consts.tf (lines 39-43) and is interpolated in plaintext into the db_app EC2 user-data (db-app.tf lines 263-266). An attacker reading the repo or the instance metadata/user-data obtains admin creds to the publicly reachable MySQL RDS.
findings.remediation: Remove the default password; require a Secrets Manager-sourced value with no default. Do not interpolate secrets into user-data; fetch at boot from Secrets Manager. Rotate the credential.

findings.title: RDS MySQL instance is publicly accessible and unencrypted
findings.attack_path: aws_db_instance.default sets publicly_accessible=true and storage_encrypted=false (db-app.tf lines 19,22) with username 'admin'. The DB endpoint resolves to a public IP; combined with the hard-coded password (TM-002) an attacker connects directly from the internet to read/modify the EMPLOYEES data with no at-rest encryption.
findings.remediation: Set publicly_accessible=false, storage_encrypted=true with a CMK, restrict the RDS security group to the app subnet, and enable backups.

findings.title: Security group web-node exposes SSH (22) and HTTP (80) to 0.0.0.0/0
findings.attack_path: aws_security_group.web-node opens ports 22 and 80 ingress to 0.0.0.0/0 (ec2.tf lines 83-96) and egress to 0.0.0.0/0. Attackers from anywhere cross the internet boundary (TB1), brute-force/exploit SSH on the public-IP instances, gaining a foothold and then using the instance profile (TM-006) to move laterally.
findings.remediation: Restrict SSH ingress to a bastion or VPN CIDR (ideally use SSM Session Manager, no port 22). Scope egress to required destinations.

findings.title: Elasticsearch domain access policy allows any AWS principal full es:* on all resources
findings.attack_path: aws_elasticsearch_domain_policy uses a document with Principal '*', Action 'es:*', Resource '*' (es.tf lines 30-43). Any AWS account can read, write, or delete indices; the domain also runs ES 2.3 with no encryption-at-rest, node-to-node encryption, or HTTPS enforcement, so data is exposed in transit and at rest.
findings.remediation: Scope the access policy to specific principals/roles and IP conditions, upgrade to a supported OpenSearch version, and enable encryption at rest, node-to-node encryption, and enforce_https.

findings.title: EC2 instance role and IAM user grant wildcard privileges (s3:*/ec2:*/rds:*/lambda:* on *)
findings.attack_path: Within the AWS account IAM boundary (TB3), ec2role policy allows s3:*, ec2:*, rds:* on Resource '*' (db-app.tf lines 210-225) and aws_iam_user_policy.excess_policy allows ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:* on '*' (iam.tf lines 25-46). After compromising an instance (TM-004) or stealing the user's access key, the attacker inherits near-admin reach over the account and pivots to every data store.
findings.remediation: Replace wildcards with least-privilege actions and resource ARNs. Remove the standing IAM user/access key in favor of role assumption with short-lived credentials.

findings.title: Public, unencrypted S3 bucket stores sensitive customer-master.xlsx
findings.attack_path: aws_s3_bucket.data is annotated 'bucket is public', is not encrypted, has no versioning or access logs (s3.tf lines 1-21) and receives customer-master.xlsx as an object (lines 23-40). Unauthenticated internet users enumerate/download the customer master file with no detection.
findings.remediation: Enable Block Public Access, apply SSE-KMS default encryption, restrict the bucket policy, and turn on versioning + access logging.

findings.title: IAM user encrypted secret access key exposed via Terraform output and committed to state
findings.attack_path: iam.tf creates a long-lived access key for aws_iam_user.user and emits the secret via output 'secret' (lines 21-54). The access key material persists in Terraform state (the S3 backend, D11); anyone reading state or output obtains durable account credentials.
findings.remediation: Avoid generating long-lived keys in Terraform. If unavoidable, never output them, encrypt and lock down state, and rotate. Prefer IAM roles.

findings.title: Stored SQL/XSS exposure in db_app PHP front-end fed by public form
findings.attack_path: The db_app user-data deploys a PHP page that accepts NAME/ADDRESS via POST and writes them to the EMPLOYEES table, rendering stored rows back to all viewers (db-app.tf lines 252-392). The page is served over plain HTTP behind the world-open SG; stored values rendered without contextual output encoding create a stored-XSS path, and the DB credential reuse amplifies tampering risk.
findings.remediation: Front the app with TLS, add output encoding for stored values, keep using parameterized/escaped queries, and restrict the app to authenticated users.

findings.title: Neptune cluster unencrypted with IAM database authentication disabled
findings.attack_path: aws_neptune_cluster.default sets storage_encrypted=false and iam_database_authentication_enabled=false (neptune.tf lines 7,9). Graph data sits unencrypted at rest and authentication is not centrally enforced through IAM, so a network-adjacent attacker (e.g., from a compromised public-subnet instance, TB2) can reach it with weaker controls.
findings.remediation: Enable storage_encrypted with a CMK and iam_database_authentication_enabled; restrict the cluster security group to the app tier.

findings.title: Classic ELB terminates plaintext HTTP only (no TLS listener)
findings.attack_path: aws_elb.weblb defines only an HTTP listener (port 80 -> instance 8000) with no HTTPS/TLS (elb.tf lines 5-10). Traffic between clients and the LB is unencrypted, allowing on-path interception or modification of application data, including any session tokens.
findings.remediation: Add an HTTPS listener with an ACM certificate and a modern TLS policy; redirect HTTP to HTTPS or migrate to an ALB.

findings.title: EKS cluster exposes public API endpoint with no encryption/logging hardening
findings.attack_path: aws_eks_cluster.eks_cluster sets endpoint_private_access=true but does not disable public access or set public_access_cidrs (eks.tf lines 122-125), so the API server remains reachable from the internet by default. No secrets encryption (envelope KMS) or control-plane logging is configured, and worker subnets auto-assign public IPs, widening the attack surface and lateral-movement options.
findings.remediation: Set endpoint_public_access=false (or restrict public_access_cidrs), enable envelope encryption of secrets with KMS, enable control-plane logging, and place nodes in private subnets.

findings.title: Unencrypted EBS volume and snapshot on public web host
findings.attack_path: aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage is created without encryption and aws_ebs_snapshot.example_snapshot copies it unencrypted (ec2.tf lines 34-69). An attacker with EC2/EBS access (granted by the wildcard role TM-006) or who shares/copies the snapshot can read its contents in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Set encrypted=true on the volume (and account-default EBS encryption), encrypt snapshots, and restrict snapshot sharing.

findings.title: RDS Aurora clusters with disabled/short backups and no encryption
findings.attack_path: rds.tf defines nine aws_rds_cluster resources; app1 has backup_retention_period=0 and app2 only 1 day (rds.tf lines 1-31), and none set storage_encrypted or kms_key_id. A destructive action or data-corruption event has no recovery window for app1, and data is unencrypted at rest.
findings.remediation: Set a non-zero backup_retention_period (>=7 days) on all clusters, enable storage_encrypted with a CMK, and enable deletion protection.

findings.title: S3 buckets (financials, operations, data_science) lack encryption/logging
findings.attack_path: aws_s3_bucket.financials and .operations have no default encryption and (financials) no logging/versioning; .data_science has no encryption (s3.tf lines 42-111). A principal abusing the wildcard s3:* permissions (TM-006) reads financial/operational data at rest in cleartext, with no access logs on financials/operations to support detection or non-repudiation.
findings.remediation: Apply SSE-KMS default encryption to all buckets, enable access logging and versioning, and enforce Block Public Access account-wide.

findings.title: KMS key used for log encryption has automatic rotation disabled
findings.attack_path: aws_kms_key.logs_key (kms.tf lines 1-16) sets no enable_key_rotation, so the CMK protecting the logs bucket (and via it, log integrity/confidentiality) is never rotated. Long-lived key material increases the value and blast radius of any future key compromise.
findings.remediation: Set enable_key_rotation=true and define a least-privilege key policy.

findings.title: ECR repository allows mutable tags with no image scanning
findings.attack_path: aws_ecr_repository.repository sets image_tag_mutability=MUTABLE and no image_scanning_configuration (ecr.tf lines 1-18). A push (via the wildcard role or the local-exec provisioner in null_resource.push_image, lines 25-35) can overwrite an existing tag with a malicious image that downstream consumers pull, and no vulnerability scanning gates the image.
findings.remediation: Set image_tag_mutability=IMMUTABLE, enable scan_on_push, and restrict push permissions to a CI principal.

findings.title: RDS security group permits unrestricted egress to 0.0.0.0/0
findings.attack_path: aws_security_group_rule.egress on the RDS SG allows all protocols/ports to 0.0.0.0/0 (db-app.tf lines 145-152). If the DB host is compromised, unrestricted egress enables data exfiltration over arbitrary protocols and C2 from the data tier.
findings.remediation: Restrict egress to the specific destinations and ports required by the workload.

findings.title: Public-subnet auto-assign public IPs place data-tier subnets on the internet edge
findings.attack_path: web_subnet/web_subnet2 and eks_subnet1/2 set map_public_ip_on_launch=true (ec2.tf lines 139,159; eks.tf lines 66,94), and a default route to the IGW (ec2.tf lines 220-228) crosses the internet boundary (TB1). Instances and the RDS subnet group placed here receive public IPs, exposing the app and (with publicly_accessible RDS) the data tier directly to the internet rather than behind a private subnet + NAT.
findings.remediation: Place application and data tiers in private subnets with map_public_ip_on_launch=false, route egress through a NAT gateway, and keep only the load balancer in public subnets.

findings.title: Lateral movement from compromised public host to data tier via shared SG and instance profile
findings.attack_path: An attacker enters via the world-open SG (E1/TB1), runs code on db_app/web_host, then (1) reads the IMDS instance-profile credentials carrying s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* (TB5/C11), and (2) reaches the RDS SG which trusts the whole VPC CIDR (db-app.tf line 141, TB2). From there they read every S3 bucket, the MySQL/Neptune/Elasticsearch stores, and operate account-wide.
findings.remediation: Scope the instance profile to least privilege, restrict the RDS SG to the specific app SG (not the VPC CIDR), require IMDSv2, and segment app vs data subnets.

findings.title: Supply-chain exposure via mutable base image build and managed AMI/runtime dependencies
findings.attack_path: null_resource.push_image builds from resources/Dockerfile (FROM python:3.7-slim, an EOL Python on a floating tag) and pushes to a mutable ECR repo (ecr.tf lines 25-35, resources/Dockerfile). A compromised or backdoored upstream base image, the most_recent amazon-linux-2 AMI, or the nodejs12.x Lambda runtime introduces untrusted code into the environment.
findings.remediation: Pin base image digests, use maintained runtimes, scan images, and verify provenance of AMIs and Lambda artifacts.

findings.title: EKS cluster network boundary lacks restriction and observability
findings.attack_path: The eks_vpc (TB4) has only public subnets and the cluster has no control-plane logging or network policy declared (eks.tf lines 44-141). An attacker who reaches a node can move within the cluster network with little segmentation and no audit trail, and the boundary between the EKS VPC and the rest of the account is not explicitly controlled.
findings.remediation: Enable EKS control-plane logging, deploy network policies, use private node subnets, and restrict cluster security-group rules.
